text.p: Shenyin & Wanguo Securities Co on Thursday said it had recommended accumulating B shares in Shanghai Worldbest Co Ltd after a surge in its 1996 profits and promising prospects in the next few years.
A Shenyin & Wanguo official said declines in the price of Worldbest's staple raw material -- polyester chips -- helped the firm's post-tax profit rise 136 percent in 1996 from 1995.

Worldbest, a textile company, issued results last week showing net profit surged to 79.087 million yuan ($9.5 million) in 1996, up from 33.555 million yuan in 1995 based on international accounting standards.
Based on domestic accounting standards, the 1996 net was 80.24 million yuan. The company had targeted a net of around 80 million yuan for 1996.
But turnover for 1996 fell more than seven percent to 405.48 million yuan from 436.731 million yuan based on domestic accounting standards, the company's annual results said.

"The fall in turnover was mainly a result of a drop in the price of raw materials pushed its major products (differential polyster filaments)," a Shenyin research paper said. "But along with the improvement of China's chemical fibre market, the company's sales will improve in 1997."
The research paper said Worldbest's short-term investments amounted to 98 million yuan in 1996, of which 20 million yuan were invested in the Worldbest Real Estate Development Co.
The remainder was used in short-term investments, the details of which were not available, the paper said.
Worldbest has invested in five major companies which are expected to bring new sources of revenue to the company, the reaserch paper said.
One investment is the purchase of 51 percent shares in Changzhou Worldbest Radici Engineering Plastic Co, a Sino-Italian joint venture now under construction.

"The joint venture is expected to begin production by the end of 1997 and is estimated to be able to contribute an annual sales turnover of 600 million yuan with a net profit of 45 million yuan," the research paper said.
